hints: Look at the displacement-time curve at $t = 0$: the particle is near extreme displacement, so ask what its gradient and speed are there.
Recall $v$ is the gradient of displacement against time and $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$, so $E_k = 0$ at peaks and troughs and maximum at each $x = 0$ crossing.
Count zero crossings in time $T$: the particle passes equilibrium twice per displacement oscillation, so the $E_k$ graph must have twice as many peaks.
walkthrough: The displacement graph shows simple harmonic vibration of period $T$: one full oscillation from $0$ to $T$ and a second from $T$ to $2T$.

Velocity is the gradient of displacement against time, $v = \frac{dx}{dt}$. At maximum positive or negative displacement the gradient is zero, so $v = 0$. At $x = 0$ the gradient is steepest, so speed $|v|$ is maximum.
Kinetic energy is $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$. Therefore $E_k = 0$ whenever $x$ is maximum, and $E_k$ is maximum whenever $x = 0$, and $E_k$ can never be negative.
At $t = 0$ the given curve is at extreme negative displacement, so $v = 0$ and $E_k = 0$. This rules out graphs starting at a maximum.

In each displacement period $T$ the particle crosses $x = 0$ twice, once in each direction. Because $E_k$ depends on $v^2$, both crossings give an $E_k$ maximum, so $E_k$ completes two cycles per $T$, with period $T/2$.
Only a graph starting at $0$, staying $\ge 0$, and showing four peaks in time $2T$ satisfies both conditions. This is option D.

A.explanation: This has maxima at $t = 0$ and period $T$. Kinetic energy cannot be maximum at maximum displacement and cannot share the displacement period $T$.

B.explanation: This is zero at $t = 0$ which is correct, but it shows only one kinetic energy cycle per displacement period $T$, whereas $v^2$ gives two maxima per period.

C.explanation: This has the correct double frequency with period $T/2$, but it shows maximum kinetic energy at $t = 0$ when the particle is at extreme displacement with zero speed.

D.explanation: Kinetic energy is zero at extreme displacement at $t = 0$ and maximum at each zero crossing, giving twice the frequency and period $T/2$ with all values $\ge 0$.
